$comment: Hatsu's decision matrix (zheref/hatsu#85, maintainer rulings of 2026-09-19). One row per condition the canon has met so far (the class is open: a human-only stop not yet recorded is still a G5). `autonomous` rows are resolved by `default` with no question and each skill states the default in one line citing the row id; `ask-once-per-run` rows ask once through the surface's picker (Crazy Slots), seeded by `preferred`; `human-gate` rows are the gates canon reserves for the maintainer and cannot be reclassified by a consumer's own file. Validated by `nen schema check` and written by `nen schema set`; read by every skill before it asks (no `nen stop` flag reads it — zheref/hatsu#289 item 8). Rows cited by a skill's one-liner: dirty-tree (breath), cap-reached (en, sharingan, senkei, build), red-lint (kokusen, gyo), missing-focused-route (kokusen, tsukuyomi), missing-tool (hanten), release-precondition-red (getsuga), semantic-conflict (ao), mode-unknown (build), stale-base (ao), staging-flag and secret-shape (kokusen), unsettled-finding (hanten), hand-edited-canon-mirror (limbo), release-go (mugetsu), canon-merge (getsuga), rewrite-published-history (aka), supply-chain-failure and host-nen-link (ten), constitution-conflict and capability-unavailable (breath section 4a: a conflicting clause, and a check that did not run), unruled-policy-surface (backlog-state), ambiguous-intent (rasengan), missing-argument and missing-configuration (every skill that takes arguments or reads configuration, WORKFLOW.md § 4 Ask, set up, continue), missing-maintainer-choice (kagutsuchi, mugetsu, izanagi, jujutsu, ren's missing request, jusshin's target, machine code and service identity; the keys it governs are its own `governs` list), stale-send (kagutsuchi section 3a), on-device-act (jujutsu; jusshin: the UAC consent, the typed service-account password, the macOS Login Items approval -- a G5 by the ruling of 2026-10-17; G5 is the open class of what only the human can do, these rows its recorded kinds), missing-tool, secret-shape and red-lint (also jusshin), wrap-up (cleanup section 2, cited at en section 8, build phase 6, futon section 10, kazaana section 7 and kamui section 8), cleanup-plan (cleanup section 6), publish-offer (kazaana section 6, mugetsu section 0 form (4)), mode-label (emperor-time section 6, dowsing-chain section 8), intake-challenger and intake-stall (emperor-time section 4, dowsing-chain section 6), ci-install-rulings and ci-ceremony (kuchiyose sections 3 and 5), harness-denied (every skill whose command a harness refuses: jutaisho section 3, WORKFLOW section Idle batches rule 2), port-siblings (kamui section 5), port-drift (bankai-rule section 5, answered for the port composites hiraishin and kamui, zheref/hatsu#357 and #356), spec-capture-scope, spec-slice, spec-clarify, spec-claim-unverified, spec-dispatch, spec-coverage, spec-conflict and spec-converge-filing (dowsing-chain sections 2, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 10; docs/config/spec-repo.md; spec-coverage raised by shibari section 4, zheref/hatsu#405). Data-only until a skill cites them: merge, signing-material, missing-consumer-declaration (tenkai, once zheref/hatsu#83's engine grows the item).

rows.default: nen shu warmup --repo <checkout> --branch <branch> --carry
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a dirty working copy at breath is always carried onto the new branch (stash including untracked, warm, restore). Nothing is discarded, the paths are listed in the report.

rows.default: scripts/send_freshness_check.sh --repo <checkout> reports at exit 2 with both SHAs named; kagutsuchi section 3b then previews and runs nen wc worktree --name kagutsuchi at origin/<branch.base>'s tip (project.fromCore repeated as --copy-from-core), rebuilds through susanoo there, re-runs the gate there, and sends from the worktree -- never from the stale checkout
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-29 (zheref/hatsu#146): a non-production upload is a release act, so the archive kagutsuchi sends must be a build of the checkout's HEAD at origin/<branch.base>'s tip, on a clean tree, asserted BEFORE --run rather than by the tag after it. A stale, dirty or foreign-commit archive is rebuilt, never a question and never sent as it stands: no maintainer answer makes a 95-commit-stale binary the right one to put in front of testers, and the maintainer's ruling is that kagutsuchi runs susanoo for a fresh build only when the latest build is not up to date with the target branch. A repository declaring no tags.identity cannot be checked (exit 3): the send proceeds and the report reads `freshness: unverified`, never `fresh`.

rows.default: nen pr request-reviews --target <owner/name> --pr <n> --add-bots <reviewer>
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19, bounded by zheref/hatsu#102; both caps are nen's keys from v0.21.0 (zheref/nen#240), and nen pr request-reviews refuses a bot's request past maxRounds at exit 2 -- exit 2 WITH a 'refused:' line is this row's bound, never retried; any other exit 2 is usage, relayed: an owed reviewer round is requested on the maintainer's behalf, through nen pr request-reviews only, while this PR's requested rounds are under nen/gates.json round_policy.maxRounds AND its resolved rounds are under round_policy.minRounds (never asked about); once minRounds resolved rounds exist no further round is requested -- 'owed at head' after the run's own push or request is not a reason -- and maxRounds with fewer resolved is the reported blocker: the run ends at not-ready with the board and nen pr ready --explain quoted, never with a question, never a number raised in-session. nen/workflow.json monitor.maxCycles is en's ACTING-cycle cap, a different number.

rows.default: into main: never merge -- en § 5's five checks in order (on branch.base, the verdict -- ready, or the sixth stop of docs/PROCESS.md section Reviewer rounds and review threads, The sixth stop (row reviewer-exhausted, under aiReviewers required), or the hanten prompt of AI reviewers per consumer (row ai-reviewers, under optional and off) --, the body, the Development guard -- WORKFLOW § Build accountability and issue associations' three exclusive cases, the PR's own base first: (1) the PR's base is the default branch, whatever branch.base declares, verified fully and its 0 required; (2) the PR's base is not the default branch and branch.base is, its retarget-pending line quoted, no prompt; (3) neither branch.base nor the PR's base is the default branch, its not-applicable line quoted in the 0's place --, the head pinned), then the merge prompt: the PR's link and the inline line gh pr merge <n> --repo <owner/name> --merge --match-head-commit <judged head>, offered for the maintainer to run or to replace with the GitHub UI, never run by the agent. Except for a recorded Futon-owned stacked delivery PR at pinned Ready, which en § 5 may merge into a non-main base through nen pr merge --delivery after its live checks. A PR off branch.base without that ownership gets no prompt: the verdict, its base and the guard's line (retarget-pending in case 2, not-applicable in case 3) are reported. A PR on branch.base in case 3 gets the prompt, the not-applicable line quoted: the G2/G4 merge stop, never a G5
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-30, docs/ROSTER.md § Rulings of 2026-09-30 -- En never merges: 'En is NOT meant to merge by default.' and 'Futon is allowed to merge by itself ONLY when target is NOT main ... (every time main is target) I should be prompted to merge myself either from the GitHub UI or from a command line offered inline.' It supersedes ruling 3 of 2026-09-29; 'main' reads as branch.base. The id is kept so existing citations resolve; it now names what happens to the run's own PR at its terminus, which is the prompt, not a merge. The class stays autonomous because the run never asks whether to merge: the prompt presents the link and the line, and its picker never carries the merge act (jutaisho § 4); the maintainer merges outside the session. Totality: a PR into branch.base, whether or not branch.base is the repository's default branch, is this row (the prompt, in case 3 with the guard's not-applicable line quoted in place of its 0) or getsuga § 3a's release proposal (rows merge and canon-merge, nen pr merge --release-unit; in case 3 § 3a does not merge and falls back to the declaration gate, which is this row's prompt); a PR off branch.base is this row's off-base report; futon's merge into its own integration branch is a local git merge --no-ff, no PR and no gate (futon § 5), so no row governs it. The 2026-10-19 Futon exception permits only recorded Ready stacked delivery PRs into non-main bases through nen pr merge --delivery; it does not alter this main-bound rule. The one PR into main an agent merges is getsuga § 3a's own release proposal, through nen pr merge --release-unit (rows merge and canon-merge). Never another's PR, never --admin or --auto.

rows.default: under nen/workflow.json aiReviewers required (the default; optional and off are row ai-reviewers): read nen pr ready --json at the judged head: nen/gates.json declares no exhaustion (reviewer_fallback is retired). A nen pr request-reviews exit 9 (unrecordedBots, zheref/nen#277) is never retried and never counted as requested, and is recorded verbatim with the headRefOid read just before the call. Where a met round_quorum fulfils an unavailable member's round (zheref/nen#361) request nothing of it and go on; where the sixth stop's five conditions hold -- docs/PROCESS.md section Reviewer rounds and review threads, The sixth stop, (a) a declared non-empty any_of, (b) failing exactly [rounds-owed], (c) every member unavailable by exit 9 or by a round-check run at the judged head that completed without a round (no run at head never counts), (d) bound to the judged head, (e) no reviewer outside any_of owed, read from owedRounds[] (HR-365); stated once there -- present the PR at en section 5's merge prompt on hanten's rounds (en section 6's sixth stop) with nen pr ready's not-ready verdict quoted verbatim, never 'ready', and the Hatsu body line carrying the recorded head and --json; any other unmet quorum stays inside sharingan section 6's bounds, and any other failing row ends at row cap-reached's terminus. A CI reviewer lane -- its round, why it is never requested, its quorum place and when it is unavailable -- is docs/PROCESS.md section Reviewer rounds and review threads, Event-driven reviewer lanes, stated once there
rows.why: Rulings 2026-10-04, 'retire 2, adopt 2' (zheref/nen#310; zheref/hatsu#227), and 2026-10-11, 'Prompt on hanten' (docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-11 -- prompt on hanten): reviewer_fallback, its chain and dated exhausted[] rows are deleted, superseded by round_quorum and zheref/nen#361; unavailability is observed (request-reviews exit 9), never declared; and when PROCESS's sixth-stop predicate holds hanten's rounds are the review and the PR goes to the maintainer's merge prompt, keeping ruling 1 of 2026-09-29's intent (docs/PROCESS.md section Reviewer rounds and review threads, One bot reviewer suffices, states it once). The run never asks. PRECEDENCE: this terminus outranks cap-reached -- an observed impossibility, not a ceiling. The verdict is nen pr ready's, quoted verbatim, never a string the verb did not print. The id is kept so existing citations resolve; the merge is the maintainer's (row own-pr-merge).

rows.default: read nen/workflow.json aiReviewers at the PR's base and at the default branch's tip through gh api contents, never the local checkout, the stricter applying (required > optional > off; a failed, absent or unparseable read is required) (required: today's behaviour -- request within round_policy's caps, expect the round, prompt only at verified Ready or docs/PROCESS.md The sixth stop; optional: request within the caps, never wait; off: never call nen pr request-reviews for reviewers[]). Under optional and off nen pr ready (nen 0.26) waives the round of a reviewer nen/gates.json declares kind bot with an identical declaration at both refs, so such a PR reads ready and goes to en section 5's merge prompt on that verified Ready, hanten having settled (zheref/hatsu#428; docs/ROSTER.md HR-333, ruled 2026-10-22). For a round nen did not waive: when nen pr ready --json at the judged head fails exactly [rounds-owed], hanten has settled, and, at both refs, every reviewers[] entry is in round_quorum.any_of with an anchored login_pattern and none is kind human (a declaration, not a bot check), present the PR at en section 5's merge prompt on hanten's rounds with the not-ready verdict quoted verbatim, never 'ready', and the Hatsu line aiReviewers: <value> (base <sha>, default <sha>); a posted bot's threads are settled first; any other failing row ends at row cap-reached's terminus. A value outside required | optional | off is missing-configuration, required applying meanwhile. The one value covers CI reviewer lanes too (ruling 2026-10-19, 'One value for every bot'): docs/PROCESS.md section Reviewer rounds and review threads, Event-driven reviewer lanes and AI reviewers per consumer, stated once there
rows.why: The maintainer's rulings of 2026-10-11 (docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-11 -- AI reviewers per consumer; zheref/hatsu#245): the per-consumer setting takes 'required | optional | off', and Hatsu's own value is 'optional'. It returns the off switch for AI-reviewer spend that deleting reviewer_fallback removed, as one consumer value rather than a dated exhaustion row. docs/PROCESS.md section Reviewer rounds and review threads, AI reviewers per consumer, states it once; under required row reviewer-exhausted's sixth stop is unchanged, under optional and off this row replaces it. Coherent with CON-16 (only enabled reviewers gate) and CON-32(b) (for a round nen did not waive, the verdict is quoted not-ready, never represented as ready; a round nen waives for a declared bot reads ready by nen's own verdict, docs/ROSTER.md HR-333). The run never asks; the merge is the maintainer's (row own-pr-merge).

rows.default: hand the tree back to hatsu:rasengan with the failing check quoted
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a red iteration check kokusen cannot clear returns to rasengan; the turn continues. It is never a G5.

rows.default: git reset --soft HEAD~1 on the tip this step just wrote (kokusen § 5) or re-squash (aka § 7), then row harness-attribution-switch for the off-switch
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-28 (zheref/hatsu#66): an ATTRIBUTION key (docs/WORKFLOW.md § commits: a trailer key ending in -by or -with, or listed in commits.forbiddenTrailers; Closes and its kind are ordinary and untouched) outside commits.allowedAttributionTrailers on a commit a Hatsu step just wrote is a harness injection (Cursor's Co-authored-by), keys compared case-insensitively as nen's layer (c) does. The just-written tip is unpublished by construction and is dropped, never amended; a published commit is row rewrite-published-history.

preferred.label: run it yourself
preferred.command: the maintainer runs the refused command, quoted verbatim in the stop, from their own shell; the run re-reads the state it produces and resumes the step after it
preferred.consequence: the step completes under the maintainer's own act; the decisions list records it

preferred.label: allow it, then re-run
preferred.command: the maintainer adds the permission rule in their own settings (never written by a skill); the run re-runs the step once
preferred.consequence: the same command runs unattended from then on (scripts/idle_permissions_check.mts lists it no longer)

preferred.label: leave it parked
preferred.command: nothing runs; the effort stays parked as g5-harness-denied
preferred.consequence: the effort stays where it stopped, named on the desk

rows.why: Zheref/hatsu#453 (HR-5; assessment D3-D5) and the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-23 on idle runs, applied by HA-PR-#460 (WORKFLOW section 2 idle: an act a default leads to that the harness refuses parks as g5-harness-denied, never retried another way); this row lands after HA-PR-#460. A command the harness refused -- its permission prompt unanswered, or its auto-mode classifier -- is an act only the maintainer can take, so it is a G5 and a human-gate row like secret-shape and on-device-act: the step ends unrun and is never retried, rephrased, split or routed through another tool; the refused command and the harness's reason are quoted verbatim; the stop is marked for the effort (nen stop --who <persona> --gate G5 --title 'harness denied: <step>' --body '<the refused command>' --mark, with --effort <branch> at nen 0.28, the pin, whose per-gate marker under <git-common-dir>/.nen/marks/ is the record; below the pin the single .nen/last-stop.json); attended, the stop is jutaisho section 4's; under --idle the effort parks (nen run park --id <run> --issue <CODE>#<N> --row g5-harness-denied, WORKFLOW section Idle batches rule 2) and the run moves on. The PR body's decisions section and the landing report list it. The 2026-10-22 delivery run met harness denials on a push, two local merges and a force-push and handed each over in prose only; this row makes each one a recorded fact with its own bell.

rows.default: ask once: the harness's commit-attribution switch is the maintainer's own configuration outside the repository, toggled by their hand; no skill writes it. On their word the dropped commit is re-run (kokusen § 5) or re-squashed (aka § 7)

preferred.label: toggle the harness switch off, then re-run the step (IDE/CLI harnesses only; on a Cursor cloud agent take B or C)
preferred.command: the maintainer toggles it (Cursor IDE/CLI only: Settings → Agent → Attribution off (Git & PRs → Attribution from Cursor 3.11), or attribution.attributeCommitsToAgent=false in ~/.cursor/cli-config.json; Cursor documents no switch for a cloud agent's Co-authored-by, docs/AGENT-ATTRIBUTION.md), then kokusen § 5 re-runs nen commit write / aka § 7 re-squashes
preferred.consequence: the re-written commit reads back clean; nothing in the repository changes. A re-run that reads the key back again means no switch reached the hook: C, before any push (zheref/hatsu#470)

preferred.label: re-run the step from a surface whose harness appends nothing
preferred.command: the same nen commit write / nen wc squash from that surface
preferred.consequence: the branch is committed there; the switch stays for the maintainer to set later

preferred.label: leave the tip dropped and stop here
preferred.command: nen stop --who Kurapika --gate G5 <efforts.md>
preferred.consequence: the change is kept unpublished — staged after kokusen § 5's drop, as the restored pre-squash commits after aka § 7; named in Not delivered

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-28 (zheref/hatsu#66, Copilot round 1 on HA-PR-#124): missing-configuration's default writes the item through its owner, which a harness file outside the repository never has; this row gives the picker an action that resumes after the maintainer toggles it.

rows.default: ask once, and only as the FALLBACK to the session-start binding (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-30, A · Reconcile, docs/ROSTER.md): scripts/nen_global.sh links the host by default. ten section 2c's offer predicate, verbatim: offered where the login shell reads installed, not reachable; never where it reads reachable; an opt-out skip is no offer (host: opted out), win32 is not read, and a removed-by-user rc entry withholds the PATH half of option A. Option A's halves follow scripts/nen_global.sh's state: where it bound the host (current, linked, kept-newer) A is the one PATH line only, never a relink (a kept-newer link is never downgraded; what the login shell resolved instead is named); where it did not (exit 2 unfixed after one rerun, 3, 4, skipped (another session is binding)) A is the link plus the PATH line; on exit 3 the statement names the real file (its path, ls -l, its --version) and that A replaces it, and the star moves to B. The session always resolves the pin -- through the host link (PATH exported in the block) or, where the host was not bound, the session bind. The login shell is the maintainer's own configuration outside the repository; ten section 2c states the exact change (one name-correct symlink on a directory the login shell already searches, pointing at a path the checksum-verified bootstrap printed, and one PATH line only where that shell's PATH lacks it) and takes it on their word only. Until then the report reads installed, not reachable

preferred.label: place the name-correct link where nen_global.sh did not bind the host, and the PATH line where it is missing (never where that rc file reads removed-by-user)
preferred.command: where nen_global.sh did not bind the host (exit 2 unfixed, 3, 4, a lock skip; on 3 replacing the real file the statement named): mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && ln -sfn <the checksum-verified binary: the path the bootstrap printed — $verified after section 2, or the verb line of section 2 run on the ok route for its printed path (a cache hit); never a path the bootstrap did not print, whatever satisfies section 1> ~/.local/bin/nen; where it did (current, linked, kept-newer) the link is left as it is, never relinked; then "$SHELL" -lic 'printf %s "$PATH"' is read and, only where it lacks $HOME/.local/bin and nen_global.sh did not report removed-by-user for that file, export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" is appended to the rc file that login shell reads (~/.zshrc for zsh, ~/.bash_profile for bash), quoted back before it is written
preferred.consequence: the probe is asked again and prints ~/.local/bin/nen with an ok row; a later bump repoints the one link and the shell line never changes. On exit 3 the recommended option is B, not this one

preferred.label: leave the host as it is; this session keeps its own binding
preferred.command: nothing is written; every pasted argv is reported as one the maintainer's shell does not resolve
preferred.consequence: the warm-up line keeps reading installed, not reachable, every session, until A is taken

rows.why: zheref/hatsu#164: the warm-up had proved nen runs for the agent while the maintainer's pasted command answered command not found. Installed and reachable are two facts; only the second is the human's, and a directory holding only the platform asset (nen-<os>-<arch>) on PATH is the trap that fails silently at the point of use, so the offer names the link, not the directory.

rows.default: hand the tree back to hatsu:rasengan to author the focused tests, then hatsu:tsukuyomi runs them
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a changed executable with no declared scoped lane gets its tests authored, never a stop and never the full suite as a substitute.

rows.default: nen shu tools --repo <checkout> --install
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a missing tool or model id is installed or resolved through the surface's own catalogue probe, never with elevation and never a version the declaration did not pin. A verify-only row that cannot be installed is reported with its remedy line and the run continues where it can.

rows.default: nen wc catch-up --repo <checkout> --base <branch.base> (ao section 3; rebase when unpublished, merge when published)
rows.why: A base that can be fast-forwarded or merged mechanically is caught up; only a semantic conflict reaches semantic-conflict.

rows.default: nen changelog collate --write, then nen changelog completeness; reconcile in the same chunk and re-run nen release preflight
rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a red release precondition (changelog completeness, uncollated fragments) is reconciled inside the same chunk of work, never a cause of stopping. An active RELEASE_HOLD and an open critical issue are not preconditions of this kind and stay human gates.

rows.default: skip ignored, large and out-of-scope paths; mention-or-skip an unmentioned deletion; commit local-config and binary paths only when the request named them
rows.why: Six of the seven nen stage triage flag kinds have a canon default; secret-shape is the seventh and is never askable (see secret-shape).

rows.default: hatsu:tenkai (apply, after its own diagnose) for a Hatsu-owned scaffolding piece

preferred.label: repair the scaffolding piece
preferred.command: scripts/tenkai_adopt.sh apply --repo <checkout>
preferred.consequence: the Hatsu-owned file is rendered; nothing routed to nen is written

preferred.label: assisted setup of the nen declaration
preferred.command: nen scaffold init --repo <checkout> --accept-detected --dry-run, then the real run after the questions are answered
preferred.consequence: the declaration lands as its own PR at G2 in a consumer repository

preferred.label: continue with the refusal quoted
preferred.command: nen shu <verb> --repo <checkout> --dry-run
preferred.consequence: the phase is reported not measurable here

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a missing declaration always gets a path forward. A Hatsu-owned scaffolding piece is repaired by tenkai without asking; a nen-routed declaration is set up through an assisted flow that asks the configuration questions itself and runs the owning verb.

rows.default: derive the value from the session, the branch, its open PRs and nen/workflow.json; one candidate a canon default covers is used and stated for this run only, otherwise ask with the candidates. Not for a maintainer's-word value; see missing-maintainer-choice

preferred.label: use the derived value
preferred.command: re-run nen parse <skill> with the line completed by the derived value, then continue
preferred.consequence: the skill runs as if the value had been typed; the turn page names where it came from

preferred.label: use the next candidate
preferred.command: re-run nen parse <skill> with the line completed by the next candidate, then continue
preferred.consequence: the same run on the other reading

preferred.label: type the value
preferred.command: the picker's free-text answer completes the line; nen parse re-runs on it
preferred.consequence: nothing runs on a guess

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-22: a missing or unparseable argument is completed inline, through the picker, and the operation continues; a refusal the maintainer has to retype around is never the outcome.

rows.default: ask per item; on the answer, set the item up through its owner, validate it with nen schema check, and resume the operation in the same turn. Nothing tracked is written unasked

preferred.label: set it up now with the detected value
preferred.command: write the item through its owner (nen scaffold init, scripts/tenkai_adopt.sh apply, hatsu:jujutsu, or the file's own key), nen schema check, then resume; a new lane, a verb argv or a project.targets entry lands through its declaration PR at that repository's gate before it runs
preferred.consequence: the configuration exists from now on; a tracked file rides this effort's branch or its own declaration PR at that repository's gate

preferred.label: set it up with another value
preferred.command: the same write with the value the maintainer picks or types
preferred.consequence: the same, on the maintainer's value

preferred.label: run once without it
preferred.command: the owning verb's --dry-run, or the phase reported not measurable here
preferred.consequence: nothing is written; the gap is named in Not delivered and asked again next time

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-22: a missing configuration item is asked for per item, written on the maintainer's behalf once answered, and the operation continues. What is not a gap is refused, never asked: WORKFLOW.md § 4 Ask, set up, continue holds the one list.
refuse: a value shaped like a secret, credential or signing material is never written: a requiresEnv-style key takes environment-variable NAMES only, and nen stage triage runs on the written file before the operation resumes (secret-shape, signing-material)
a frozen or foreign registry (a reference repository, another owner's nen/repos.json) is reported, never written

preferred.label: type the value
preferred.command: the maintainer types the value as free text; the declared candidates are listed for reference, none starred, none a picker option that performs the act
preferred.consequence: the line is completed with the typed value and nen parse re-runs on it

preferred.label: stop here
preferred.command: end the run with the plan printed and nothing acted on
preferred.consequence: nothing runs; the operation resumes when the maintainer types the value

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-23: a value that is the maintainer's own word (a target, a go, a cap, a device, the request) is typed, never picked and never derived. No default and no recommended option: a default is a derivation and a starred option is a pick. The declared candidates may be listed for reference, none starred, and none is ever an option that performs the act. mugetsu asks only for the destination, on the maintainer's own same-turn hatsu:mugetsu that names none where several are declared; the go itself is never asked (mugetsu § 0), and every other reach prints the plan and stops. Ruling 2026-09-30 (docs/ROSTER.md, Rulings of 2026-09-30 -- jusshin) extends the class to jusshin's target repository, the machine code every runner on a host is named by, and the service identity its services log on as; <target> and <machine> are grammar slots, and <service-identity> is typed like jujutsu <device>, completing the elicitation rather than the line. Ruling 2026-10-04 adds jusshin's <accept-daily-account> word. Its <desktop-overlap> answer is historical: nen 0.21 and Hatsu#204 give every pool its own label, so that overlap no longer arises.

preferred.label: Transmuter (machinery)
preferred.command: proceed in Transmuter mode
preferred.consequence: workflows, scripts, hooks, generators; G4 in a canon repository

preferred.label: Conjurer (canon and governance)
preferred.command: proceed in Conjurer mode
preferred.consequence: constitution, handbooks, skill prose; G4 in a canon repository

preferred.label: Enhancer (product code)
preferred.command: proceed in Enhancer mode
preferred.consequence: product source and tests; G2

rows.why: The mode is derived from the issue's labels and the diff's paths first; the picker fires only on a genuine tie.

preferred.label: take ours
preferred.command: git checkout --ours -- <path> && git add <path>
preferred.consequence: the branch's meaning wins on this hunk

preferred.label: take theirs
preferred.command: git checkout --theirs -- <path> && git add <path>
preferred.consequence: the base's meaning wins on this hunk

preferred.label: a genuine third resolution the run proposes
preferred.command: apply the shown patch, then git add <path>
preferred.consequence: both meanings are kept as the run describes

preferred.label: resolve it and show me the diff before anything is committed
preferred.command: resolve, then git diff --cached -- <path>; commit only after the maintainer reads it
preferred.consequence: the run types, the maintainer decides

rows.why: Ruling 2026-09-19: a semantic conflict in ao always goes to Crazy Slots with both sides shown verbatim and these four options; the run never picks a side.

preferred.label: extend scope and take the proposed fix
preferred.command: apply the reviewer's proposed fix
preferred.consequence: the change set grows by the finding

preferred.label: adopt the business rule the finding implies
preferred.command: record the rule in the PR body and apply it
preferred.consequence: a new rule, stated where it can be reviewed

preferred.label: keep the durable pending record and stop
preferred.command: hatsu:file with the finding as evidence
preferred.consequence: the finding outlives the branch as an issue

rows.why: hanten section 7: only after the four-fact test proves none of section 6's dispositions can be chosen without the maintainer.

preferred.label: the edit is canon: file it upstream, then regenerate
preferred.command: hatsu:file with the mirror file's diff as evidence, against the canonical handbooks repository (G4 there); then hatsu:limbo for <path> as sync
preferred.consequence: the mirror returns to the canon's bytes; the rule lives on as an issue where canon is authored

preferred.label: the edit is repo-specific: move it to the consumer's own file, then regenerate
preferred.command: move the content to a file the mirror does not own (a subdirectory of the rules directory, CLAUDE.md, prose outside the AGENTS.md block); then hatsu:limbo for <path> as sync
preferred.consequence: the consumer keeps its rule as its own; the mirror is the canon again

preferred.label: the file is a predecessor generator's mirror: remove it, then regenerate
preferred.command: git rm the files whose first line is the predecessor's marker; then hatsu:limbo for <path> as sync
preferred.consequence: nothing is lost -- the canon at the pin is the source; every surface carries nen's marker from now on

rows.why: limbo section 3: a hand-edited mirror file means a rule was written into the mirror instead of the canon, and nen canon mirror generate would overwrite a marked one silently (an unmarked one it refuses whole, exit 2, nothing written). Where the rule belongs -- canon, the consumer's own file, or nowhere because the file was a retired generator's -- is the maintainer's to say; limbo names the files and stops before any write. C is starred in the picker only for a file whose first line is the predecessor's marker.

No PR into main is merged by an agent in this plane, the run's own included: every one ends at en § 5's merge prompt (row own-pr-merge, docs/ROSTER.md § Rulings of 2026-09-30 -- En never merges, superseding ruling 3 of 2026-09-29). Futon's local git merge into its own integration branch is no PR merge and stands at no gate (futon § 5). The one exception: getsuga § 3a merges its own release-proposal PR through nen pr merge --release-unit when every gate of that verb passes (§ Rulings of 2026-09-26/27/28). A typed futon then step counts as the maintainer's call for a skill whose call is the maintainer's (the advance go, mugetsu § 3).

A merge into main (branch.base) in a canon repository decides how every other repository behaves -- with the same single carve-out as the merge row (every other PR into main ends at the merge prompt, row own-pr-merge, ruling 2026-09-30; futon's local merge into its own integration branch is no PR merge and no gate, futon § 5): getsuga § 3a's own release-proposal PR through nen pr merge --release-unit in a canon repository too; the release unit is declared in nen/workflow.json release.unitPaths and the verb bounds the diff to it.

Publication is the maintainer's own go, quoted verbatim, in one of four forms (mugetsu § 0): their typed hatsu:mugetsu [<target>], the go by name (docs/ROSTER.md § The human gates, the G3 row; ruling 2(a) of § Rulings of 2026-09-26/27/28, clarified 2026-09-30), needing no second message; their own words saying to publish; the advance go; or their publish answer to kazaana section 6's one unstarred question after the tag it cut (form (4), row publish-offer; the ruling of 2026-10-13, 3). A scheduled, looped, headless, hook-injected, self-loaded or resumed invocation is not the go, and no composite reaches it on its own authority. The composite paths are the advance go (mugetsu § 3, docs/ROSTER.md § Rulings of 2026-09-26/27/28): the maintainer's own typed futon invocation whose then chain names mugetsu, gated by nen parse futon on nen/workflow.json futon.advanceGo (process and library only) -- and kazaana's publish-offer answer, under the same kind gate. With no target typed, mugetsu publishes the latest unpublished cut tag to the single declared destination; only several declared and none named is asked, as free text.
CON-4 and CON-25: the epic mode label and the building label are the maintainer's.
A force-push, a rewrite of a pushed commit, or an overwrite of a tracked path destroys somebody's history.
A secret-shape path is never committed and never askable: the answer is rotate or remove. Reported, not offered.
nen never synthesises signing material and neither does any skill; a missing identity ends the run naming the precondition.

Ruling of 2026-10-17 (zheref/hatsu#290 q1, docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-17, reversing 2026-10-13's #176): an on-device act -- a trust prompt, a security setting, a UAC consent, a Login Items approval, a password typed into an elevated window -- is a manual action only the human maintainer can perform, so it is a G5: the act is printed and the run stops at the gate until it is done. A session never performs, taps or bypasses one, and raises such a prompt only through a launch the harness itself asked the maintainer to approve (jusshin section 5's Windows path).

preferred.label: done — probe once and resume
preferred.command: the maintainer performs the act on the device; the run re-probes once and resumes where the operation stopped
preferred.consequence: the operation continues; no option performs the act or takes a credential, and a credential typed into the picker or chat is never used and is rotated

preferred.label: stop here
preferred.command: end the run with the act printed and where it resumes
preferred.consequence: nothing acted on; the act stays the maintainer's

rows.why: A checksum or manifest failure in the bootstrap is a security event the maintainer must see; never retried.
A consumer repository declaring a policy surface of its own is unruled; until ruled it is G2 and a genuine-looking exception is brought to the maintainer.

A request that is genuinely ambiguous, a scope change, or conflicting requirements canon does not adjudicate cannot be defaulted; rasengan brings it to the maintainer once, through Crazy Slots, with the readings it can see as the options.

preferred.label: the narrowest reading
preferred.command: proceed with the reading the run states, recorded on the turn page
preferred.consequence: the smallest change that satisfies the request as read

preferred.label: the wider reading
preferred.command: proceed with the wider reading the run states
preferred.consequence: more surface changes; named in the PR body

preferred.label: restate the request
preferred.command: stop; the maintainer restates
preferred.consequence: nothing authored on a guess

rows.default: leave the axis empty; list the issue as undecidable with the reason in the classify table; a later run picks it up
rows.why: Ruling 2026-10-04: an axis the classifier cannot decide with confidence is never filled with a best guess -- nen's own undecidable discipline (effort classify). Low-confidence keys are listed and never applied by hatsu:classify; nen classify apply --include-low exists for the maintainer's own hand.

rows.default: ask once when the session's surface, model alias or effort (compared in the surface's own dial) is outside the SET of hatsu:direct's picks -- the primary, the recommended and the fallback (contracts/direct.registry.json -> mismatch.within); a session on the recommended or the fallback is one line, `within the registry's set`, never asked; an unread session value is never a mismatch; the recommendation is for the maintainer's own session and never blocks build or ren (the maintainer's rulings of 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-05: the typed hatsu:build or hatsu:ren is already the decision to work here)

preferred.label: continue here, on this model and effort
preferred.command: nen direct answer --record <effort id> --answer continue --repo <checkout>, then continue the build without another word
preferred.consequence: the work runs where it was started; the verdict and the mismatch stay in the ledger and the report

preferred.label: stop so I restart on the primary's surface
preferred.command: nen direct answer --record <effort id> --answer stop --repo <checkout>; end the run naming the restart line direct quoted (surfaces.<s>.restart, its placeholders filled from models.<surface>.<tier> and effort.surfaceMap only)
preferred.consequence: nothing is authored here; the maintainer opens the primary's surface and types hatsu:build (or hatsu:ren) there

rows.why: Ruling 2026-10-04: direct advises, never gates -- a mismatch is asked once through the picker with continue starred, and a build is never blocked from starting on a non-recommended model or effort. Ruling 2026-10-05: the compare runs against the whole set of picks, so a session already on the cost-agnostic recommended or the cost-aligned fallback pick is within the registry and is told so in one line.

rows.default: ask once per run, every unmapped row of the port batched into ONE picker call -- three questions a call, a fourth row opens a second call in the same run, never a question per row (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-19/20, zheref/hatsu#354: 'Ask once, record ruling'); each question names the source rule or concept and the target stack; the answer binds the current port the moment it is given and becomes one row with a reserved id in the ports pair file through hatsu:bankai-rule sections 3-4 (asked by the port composites hatsu:hiraishin and hatsu:kamui), on the run's rulings branch. Before asking, the spec's private '## Platform decisions' section is read (docs/config/ports.md, Product-level divergence): a row already answering the concept for the same platform is cited, never asked; a concept no entry of ports.md's mirror-versus-map list names is 'unclassifiable' and asked here, never classified by the agent. Option A is starred ONLY when its equivalent is quoted from an existing pair row or an explicit handbook cross-reference, its source line shown; an agent-derived equivalent is listed unstarred with its source line and C is starred. The star is set per ask, never statically: no option of this row carries 'recommended'. The pair row's rationale is the picked label or the maintainer's typed words verbatim, byte-equal to the answer, and never names a product, screen, business rule or object id; its redraft is the technology-level restatement, shown before/after in the plan before kokusen; words naming a product go, under a composite with a spec folder, to the spec's '## Platform decisions' row in the same run with the handling label as the rationale, and are otherwise refused from the pair file with a technology-level restatement asked (hatsu:bankai-rule section 1)

preferred.label: map to <equivalent> (source line shown)
preferred.command: hatsu:bankai-rule <from> to <to> ruling <source> maps to <the equivalent> -- shown with its source line; starred only when quoted from an existing pair row or an explicit handbook cross-reference
preferred.consequence: an equivalence row, handling map; the port implements the equivalent

preferred.label: mirror
preferred.command: hatsu:bankai-rule <from> to <to> ruling <source> mirrors as-is
preferred.consequence: an equivalence row, handling mirror; the port carries the source rule unchanged

preferred.label: drop with note
preferred.command: hatsu:bankai-rule <from> to <to> ruling <source> dropped: <why, technology-level>
preferred.consequence: a drift row; the port leaves it out and the PR says so

preferred.label: target-only addition
preferred.command: hatsu:bankai-rule <from> to <to> ruling target adds <concept>
preferred.consequence: a drift row; the port adds what the target stack needs and the source never had

rows.why: Ruling 2026-10-19/20 (zheref/hatsu#354, 'When a source change has no target equivalent?' -> 'Ask once, record ruling'; the challenge settlement 'port-drift per row' -> one batched picker call per run): a drift is the maintainer's decision, asked once and recorded as canon so the next port never asks it again; four handlings and no fifth (bankai-rule section 4). SDD plan 2026-10-22 (porting-drift): a pre-starred agent-derived equivalent became append-only canon on one tap, and one rationale field held both the maintainer's words and the agent's redraft -- so the star is earned by a quoted source, and the row keeps both side by side.

rows.default: read nen/workflow.json -> intake.challenger from Hatsu's own checkout ($hatsu_root), never the target's, and raise in emperor-time section 4 every intake examiner whose artifact the brief matches (brief -> satotz, spec -> lippo, platform -> buhara, rendered -> bisky as Hatsu's value; HR-24, HR-25, HR-38), with no question; a key missing from the map names no examiner for that artifact, which goes to satotz, said in the run (HR-26). Only where intake.challenger itself is absent or not an object, or a value is outside the intake cast, does the run ask, once per run and per artifact, the star on that artifact's HR-24 examiner (derived per ask; no option below is statically starred); the answer binds that run and is NEVER written by it (Hatsu's value changes by a G4 PR through scripts/config_values.sh set). A code reviewer (a hanten persona) or kurapika is never a value and re-asks (HR-23); a persona with no definition is hanten section 3's gap, that part unchallenged, said. The map routes challenges only: bisky drafts the Design Direction and satotz challenges it, by name, whatever the map says (HR-27, HR-31)

preferred.label: Satotz
preferred.command: raise hatsu:satotz as docs/INTAKE-CHALLENGE.md section 3 states, title emperor-time · satotz · <alias>
preferred.consequence: the brief's problem, audience, criteria, priority and scope boundaries, and Bisky's Design Direction (HR-31)

preferred.label: Lippo
preferred.command: raise hatsu:lippo the same way
preferred.consequence: the spec: edge cases, error and boundary states, conflicts with the specification in force

preferred.label: Buhara
preferred.command: raise hatsu:buhara the same way
preferred.consequence: the platforms: each platform's constraints, parity, the stack

preferred.label: Bisky
preferred.command: raise hatsu:bisky the same way
preferred.consequence: the rendered parts, after her Design Direction draft (HR-27)

rows.why: Added with hatsu:emperor-time (2026-10-19) to ask while OPEN-4 was open; rewritten when OPEN-4's rulings landed (docs/ROSTER.md HR-23 ... HR-38): the challenger is a dedicated intake cast isolated from code review, declared as a map from artifact to examiner (HR-21), every matching examiner challenging (HR-25). The ask remains only for an absent or out-of-set value; the star is derived per ask, that artifact's HR-24 examiner. docs/INTAKE-CHALLENGE.md section 1.

rows.default: ask once per kamui run, after its spec PR reads MERGED, through the surface's picker: which of the product family's configured siblings (every families[].members entry of the spec repository's default-branch nen/repos.json, kamui section 2, but the source repository) receive a port issue. Multi-select, NO option starred (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-19/20, zheref/hatsu#354: "Always ask through a picker which of all the configured siblings the new implementation should be ported to." -- a recorded exception to jutaisho section 4's one star); paged in fours, a fifth item opening a second call; under three items the picker carries the items plus none of them, and an empty answer reads none of them; a lone sibling is still asked, never auto-picked; zero siblings is said and the run goes to kamui section 8. A sibling whose scenario bankai-handbooks does not govern is listed marked handbook-question (CON-37) and dropped if picked, said. The answer is the G1 for the filings (file section 4's clause, landing with zheref/hatsu#355): one port issue per picked sibling through file sections 3-5, an existing one amended, never filed twice The answer is the G1 for the filings under file section 4's composite clause (zheref/hatsu#355, landed with HA-PR-#367; docs/config/ports.md, Shared conventions).

preferred.label: port to the siblings picked
preferred.command: per picked sibling: file sections 3-5 by name (the four searches, the plan, the labels and section 5's one direct run), then nen issue file --target <owner/name> --repo <sibling checkout> --assignee <maintainer> ... --private-names-ignore-file <file section 4's ignore file> --json, read back with gh issue view
preferred.consequence: one port issue per picked sibling, each linking the merged spec folder and the source object; then kamui section 7's start picker

preferred.label: none of them
preferred.command: nothing is filed; the run goes to kamui section 8 (the register and the wrap-up), next done
preferred.consequence: the spec stands merged; no sibling receives a port issue; a later hatsu:kamui on the same source amends the same spec folder

rows.why: Added with hatsu:kamui (zheref/hatsu#356) under the epic's rulings (zheref/hatsu#354): the siblings are always picked by the maintainer, so no option is recommended -- like publish-offer, a consumer's own decisions file may not star an option or give this row a default that skips the question -- advisory: no guard enforces it yet, the same as publish-offer.

rows.default: ask once, and only when BOTH prerequisites hold (cleanup section 2; docs/ROSTER.md HR-366, zheref/hatsu#480): (1) every pull request in the sitting's scope reads MERGED on a live read -- an unread merge state never counts as merged, and a PR the maintainer closed unmerged leaves the scope (HR-367) -- and (2) the maintainer has explicitly declared the sitting satisfied, in their own words, quoted in the report. Readiness, green checks, en section 5's merge prompt, a composite's run ending, a merge alone, silence, a configured default and an unattended run never supply (2); short of both, no picker is shown, no cleanup runs, and the report names the missing prerequisite. The callers, each at its terminus: Kurapika as main session after en section 8, build phase 6, futon section 10, kazaana section 7, kamui section 8, hiraishin section 8, backlog-loop section 10, dowsing-chain section 11. Under --idle (2) is never met, so this row and cleanup-plan read refuse (HR-366, ruled 2026-10-26; a floor futon_effort_record.mts start enforces) and an idle run neither offers nor runs cleanup. When both hold, through the surface's own picker: cleanup, cleanup and third-hand in parallel, or continue iterating. cleanup is REQUIRED after a completed session and third-hand is optional (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-13, docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-13, 5). The wrap-up names no human-called phase (aka, mukai, the merge, kagutsuchi, mugetsu) and is never a merge prompt. A section 7 marker reading cleaned, none-proposed or already-clean is completed: cleanup is not re-asked and B is offered as third-hand alone (cleanup section 2). When a terminus finds a prerequisite missing it names it with the resume words; a later declaration in the maintainer's own message has Kurapika as main session re-read every scoped PR live and ask once when all read MERGED; no agent solicits the declaration; a maintainer-typed hatsu:cleanup is their own word and runs under cleanup section 1, outside this offer

preferred.label: run cleanup
preferred.command: hatsu:cleanup -- Shizuku inventories this sitting and every prior leftover, returns the plan, the maintainer picks (row cleanup-plan), she removes only the pick
preferred.consequence: what the effort left behind, locally and remotely, is swept; the sitting closes with the sweep reported

preferred.label: run cleanup and third-hand in parallel
preferred.command: hatsu:cleanup and hatsu:third-hand, raised side by side (Shizuku and Netero each in two passes, each filing or removing only the maintainer's pick)
preferred.consequence: the sweep and the 0-3 harvested process issues, both on the maintainer's picks; the sitting closes

preferred.label: continue iterating on this session
preferred.command: nothing runs; the next request is a ren turn on the same effort
preferred.consequence: nothing is swept; the offer returns at the maintainer's next explicit declaration of satisfaction, every scoped PR then reading MERGED (cleanup section 2)

rows.why: Ruling 2026-10-13: running cleanup is always required after a completed session and is offered once a single PR lands as a session delivery; third-hand remains optional; the maintainer may run cleanup, cleanup and third-hand in parallel, or continue iterating. This amends ruling 1 of 2026-09-09 (no agent prompts for the five phases -- neither offer here is one of them) and third-hand section 2's never-ask rule. Corrected 2026-10-25 by the maintainer (zheref/hatsu#480): 'Cleanup should never be offerered if PRs in scope are not merged and the sitting has been determined satisfied by maintainer.' Read as two independent prerequisites (docs/ROSTER.md HR-366, a reading): the trigger above replaces the 2026-10-13 ruling's 'offered once a single PR lands as a session delivery', whose words stand as the dated record.

rows.default: present Shizuku's plan as ONE lettered question through the surface's own picker: A every deterministic row (a mechanical fact decides -- a merged PR's clean worktree, its remote head where git ls-remote returns the PR's headRefOid, then the worktree and its merged branch; a prunable entry; this sitting's returned hanten-/prove- checkouts; a stale tracking ref; <reports.dir>/current.html), B those plus the proposed rows the maintainer ticks next, asked in batches of at most three per question where the surface caps options (uncommitted work with every path listed, a closed-unmerged or PR-less branch, a merged remote head whose SHA moved, a merged branch with no worktree, a merged effort's captures, a build cache in a kept worktree, a prior session's detached checkouts, a cache binary below the pin with its spelled rm), C none. Named rows (billed resources, the surface's own worktrees, a locked or open-PR worktree, a refused name) are listed and never an option. NOTHING is removed before the answer; none wins over every other tick; pass 2 runs only the picked rows in cleanup section 5's order, each remote delete from its worktree before that worktree goes, each read back with the bytes freed (cleanup sections 5-6)

preferred.label: apply the deterministic rows
preferred.command: every deterministic row, in cleanup section 5's order: git worktree prune; per merged clean worktree git -C <wt> push origin --delete -- <branch> (only when git ls-remote returns the PR's headRefOid), then git worktree remove -- <wt>, then git branch -d -- <branch>; this sitting's returned hanten-/prove- checkouts; git remote prune origin; rm -- <reports.dir>/current.html -- each followed by its read-back
preferred.consequence: what a fact says is dead is gone; every proposed and named row is kept and named in the report

preferred.label: apply the deterministic rows and the proposed rows I tick
preferred.command: the same, then the proposed rows asked in batches of at most three per question where the surface caps options; each ticked row's exact command as the plan spelled it; a named row is never asked
preferred.consequence: the ticked judgement calls are performed too; an unticked or named one is kept and named

preferred.label: none -- keep everything
preferred.command: nothing runs; the marker records none-picked
preferred.consequence: the inventory stands in the report; the leftovers are offered again at the next wrap-up

rows.why: Ruling 2026-10-13: Shizuku offers an action plan split between deterministic and non-deterministic proposed operations to free storage and resources and ensure maximum hygiene, covering prior sessions' leftovers as encountered; she never destroys before the pick and never a tree she has not inspected (dirty-tree's discipline), and the .nen/ ledgers are the record, never a leftover.

rows.default: ask once, after kazaana's getsuga step cut the tag and git ls-remote --tags origin resolves it, and ONLY where nen repo classify's kind is listed under nen/workflow.json -> futon.advanceGo.mugetsu (process, library; a product repository's publication stays typed by name, said): Publish <tag> through hatsu:mugetsu to <the single declared destination>? No option is starred -- G3 is never recommended. The affirmative answer is the maintainer's own go, form (4) of mugetsu section 0, quoted verbatim with the question's text in the report and on the release PR (the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-13, docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-13, 3); several destinations declared and none named is mugetsu section 3's free-text ask. The go lapses with the run

preferred.label: publish -- this answer is my go for hatsu:mugetsu on this tag
preferred.command: hatsu:mugetsu [<target>] with this answer quoted as the go: nen release preflight, then nen shu release and/or nen shu deploy --target <production target> --run, one target once
preferred.consequence: the release is published to that one destination; the go and the question are quoted on the release PR

preferred.label: not now -- the tag stands
preferred.command: nothing runs; the report names the tag and the line to type later (hatsu:mugetsu [<target>])
preferred.consequence: nothing publishes; a later typed hatsu:mugetsu is its own go

rows.why: Ruling 2026-10-13: once the tag is cut successfully, offer the maintainer through a picker whether mugetsu should be started to publish a new release under the last cut tag in the session. This is the one question an agent asks about G3: mugetsu section 1's no-agent-ever-prompts and missing-maintainer-choice's typed-never-picked are amended for this question alone; the gate itself (row release-go) is unchanged and the answer is the maintainer's own word, never starred, never derived. Because the answer crosses G3, this row is bound like a human-gate row: a consumer's own decisions file may not reclassify it, give it a default, or star an option (docs/config/decisions.json.md section The three row classes). The kind gate is the target's futon.advanceGo.mugetsu as nen parse futon reads it (declared, or nen's default where absent) on the target's nen repo classify kind; zero declared destinations is no offer; several are one unstarred option each.

preferred.label: continue
preferred.command: re-raise every stalled examiner, active, for another round (docs/INTAKE-CHALLENGE.md section 4)
preferred.consequence: the loop goes on; no round is counted (HR-29)

preferred.label: stop and go on with the open questions
preferred.command: emperor-time section 5 on the brief as it stands
preferred.consequence: the brief is filed only on section 6's confirmation, every unsettled challenge an open question in it, the maintainer's at G1 (HR-32)

rows.why: The stop: in emperor-time section 4's challenge loop, when no intake examiner remains active and at least one has stalled -- its round amended, answered or withdrew none of its challenges and raised no new one (HR-35) -- ask the maintainer through the picker, at EVERY such stop, never defaulted (HR-30, HR-36); each stalled examiner's unsettled challenges are already open questions in the brief (HR-37). Rulings of 2026-10-21 (docs/ROSTER.md HR-29, HR-30, HR-32 ... HR-37): intake challenge rounds are never counted, a stall is judged per examiner and drops that examiner, and the maintainer's stop is the loop's only bound -- a ruled exception, for the intake challenge alone, to izanagi section 6 and en's cap limit. Human-gate because the maintainer is asked at every all-stalled stop (HR-36).

rows.default: ask once per capture run, after dowsing-chain section 2 folds the members' inventory rows into one capability map (one row per user-facing capability reachable from navigation or a feature flag, a generic slug proposed for each): which capabilities this run captures. A capability already holding a folder on the spec repository's origin/<base> routes to recapture, never capture. The answer is recorded in the run record's scope[] and binds this run only

preferred.label: all <N> capabilities
preferred.command: capture every capability on the map, in waves of spec.capture.foldersPerPr folders
preferred.consequence: one spec PR per wave at G2 until the map is captured

preferred.label: only the slugs I type
preferred.command: capture the typed slugs, each checked against the map and the slug pattern of docs/config/spec-repo.md
preferred.consequence: the rest of the map stays uncaptured and is listed on the desk

rows.why: Added with hatsu:dowsing-chain (ROSTER HR-12, HR-16; the SDD plan's piece P10), the capture skill's design as authored; docs/config/spec-repo.md, The pickers. The scope is the maintainer's to narrow; the whole map is the default because a partial canon is the drift the skill exists to end.

rows.default: ask once per run, three questions a call (a fourth opens a second call in the same run), for each screen or state the inventory reaches from two capabilities: which capability's folder specifies it. The star is derived per ask: the capability whose navigation edge reaches it first in the reference platform's inventory; none when no reading is cited. The answer is written to the folder's research.md with the rows it moved

preferred.label: <the capability whose navigation edge reaches it first>
preferred.command: specify it in that capability's folder; the other folder cites it by FR id
preferred.consequence: one owner folder, one cross-reference

preferred.label: <the other capability>
preferred.command: specify it in the other folder; the first cites it by FR id
preferred.consequence: one owner folder, one cross-reference

preferred.label: its own capability folder

The star is derived per ask (the reading a declared-tier citation carries); NONE is starred where the answer is a priority, an audience, a threshold or 'intentional' (WORKFLOW section 4, the maintainer's word is never derived). The ci catalogue rows carry ownedBy: kuchiyose, so config_values diagnose, fill and need never list them and tenkai never asks or fills them; the class is human-gate so no consumer file can turn HR-137's per-consumer ask into a default.

rows.why: Added with hatsu:kuchiyose (zheref/hatsu#331). The day-one ceremony -- creating each -akatsuki GitHub App with its permission tier and installing it (HR-138), setting its App id and private-key secrets and the Claude auth secret (HR-139), the Hidan variable, and applying the ruleset that registers the lane checks as required status checks (HR-140: printed, never applied) -- is account-level identity creation, secret material and a repository security setting: a permission, secret or settings change only the human can make, a G5 under CON-47 (HR-138, HR-140; the provider's docs/provisioning/RUNBOOK.md, Human gates). CON-12 fixes only the shape -- one least-privilege App per lane at its tier. The install PR itself stands at the consumer's declaration gate, CON-5 (G2) or CON-7 (G4) as nen repo classify answers, and is never merged by the run. The run prints one block per step and waits; no option performs a step or takes a credential, and a secret value typed into the picker or chat is never used and is rotated. Secret steps run in the maintainer's own terminal, never the session (the private key by stdin, the downloaded .pem deleted); the ruleset payload is printed inline with its sha256 for the maintainer to check; the permission pack denies the session gh secret set/delete, gh variable set and gh api writes to rulesets, secrets and variables.
